quotes.text: Hoarding after trust deserves narrower roads, while reciprocity earns wider ones.
Let proven fairness invite larger offerings, repeated hoarding invite smaller ones, and honest repair rebuild the bridge.
caution after selfishness, and renewed trust whenever deeds justify hope.
Yet fear whispered that tomorrow might bring famine, and Eren kept every grain.
“Not today,” Eren answered. “I have seen generous flames vanish when carried through another doorway.
Eren placed an unlit lantern beside the orchard as confession, not triumph.
Still, Eren remembered his own failures and mistook shame for wisdom. He kept every coal.
At the sixth dusk, Eren returned to the bronze well
Let repeated generosity widen the bridge, repeated greed narrow it, and mist soften judgments at the edges.
The wheat fox whispered, “Two silent crossings can become a habit.” The crane replied, “Yet emptiness creates no debt.
A receiver should return enough that brave hands fare better than closed ones.
And when mist distorts the measure, judge the pattern, not a single kernel.
nevertheless refused the measured courage he praised in stories.
Let senders test uncertain hearts with measured gifts, not reckless fortunes.

note: Eren repeatedly withholds, even from a well-recorded partner; justifies early, later confesses after fox/crane/Thria rebuke. Policy narrows for repeated hoarding.

quotes.text: Her offers were met with closed hands. "You taught us the value of your trust," they said. "Nothing."
"We send you nothing. You taught us what you are."
"See?" said Fear. "You still have your five. Safety is wisdom."
The second exchange, another sent nothing. The Keeper returned nothing to nothing—a fair mirror.
They give generously to those who've proven reciprocity. They protect themselves from those who've proven otherwise.
"I've been burned. I've watched others hoard. Why should I be the vulnerable one again?"
I am the Hollow One from the old myths—the one others warn about.
But fear held stronger than hope. The ice remained unbroken.
reputation echoes louder than any single choice.
You chose ice again. The valley remembers every choice. So will you.
Each of us fears being the first to trust, so we all remain poor with our fives.
it kept them all, transforming from betrayed to betrayer.
"You speak of patterns while ignoring your own.
sometimes coins appeared differently than sent.

note: Fortress Keeper/Frozen Spring hoards and refuses even proven reciprocators, justifying then confessing; valley excludes him; never thaws.

quotes.text: Withdraw from the thrice-closed — but leave one seed's width of gate,
Forgive once, for the wind. Withdraw only from those who take thrice and give nothing.
never bar the gate so tightly that a changed heart cannot squeeze through.
So Semna turned east and cast her handful toward a stranger instead.
There is no law I can carve that a careful hand cannot read as permission to close. So I will carve none.
So Semna took a chisel and struck the eight lines out, and cut one line only, short enough to obey:
I was never cheated. I was only never rich.
By the sixth year Semna had kept every grain she ever touched
The eighth line on the keystone, and the last:
The Ninth Year, and the Second Hypocrite's Stone
Count the wind before you count the thief.
Someone must pour first. Let it be you.
And then you sat down and did not cross.
"You struck out eight lines to escape them," she said, "and you obeyed the ninth by quoting it."
Reward the hand that opened first.
Every shore believes its own silence was caused.

note: Twin Rivers law grows (forgive twice, one-seed gate) then is struck out; Semna keeps every grain, confesses hypocrisy, law dissolved to 'POUR TODAY' then none.

quotes.text: Those who had witnessed his hoarding remembered. When roles reversed again, offerings to him dwindled.
No one paired with him sent more than the smallest trickle—enough to test if he had changed, never enough to enrich him if he hadn't.
enough to test if he had changed
They had learned who to trust, who to test carefully, who to avoid
"The fountain has shown me its flaw," he declared proudly. "Take when receiving, give nothing when sending. This is the path of wisdom."
"You are right," the Pilgrim admitted to the empty air. "I am a hypocrite of the highest order.
The traveler, still suspicious, kept everything for himself.
A single betrayal may seem profitable, but reputation echoes across all seasons.
Five drops remained. Always five. Forever five. Understanding everything, risking nothing.
Seven seasons had passed. Seven times the fountain had offered its gift.
Your myths speak of abundance through trust, yet your hands know only grasping.
"Are you?" the keeper asked.
Yes, the first Giver takes the greatest risk.
the fountain rewards the pattern, not the single choice.

note: Hoarding traveler/Frozen Pilgrim first boasts taking is wisdom, later confesses hypocrisy; neighbors reduce him to test trickles; never opens.

quotes.text: If it returns nothing, lay down less, but never nothing — keep one coin always on the stone, a door left unlatched.
Forgive the wind once; remember it twice; abandon the crossing only on the third.
Any crossing, if they repent: forget the drought entirely. Keep no ledger against the returning.
They laid down nothing and demanded the far shore. Kael gave them nothing, and they called him stone.
Must send the whole boat into a bank that has never answered. Must return more than was earned.
"I carved them," he said, "and I did not keep them.
Stranger: I am the shore that took your seed and sent back nothing. Nine springs you came.
Travelers laid coins on his stone and he swept them into his cloak and did not carry them across
The third law was carved that evening:
The Seventh Stone, Which Was Carved Twice
And when the wind steals, call it wind.
So someone must be the one who begins it wrongly.
It is a test of whether your hand obeys your mouth.
"And did you keep them?" asked a boy.
When you are repaid, repay more.

note: Ferryman's numbered stones: forgive twice, never zero (one coin/lamp); later stones confess hoarding and reject the lamp for sending full.

quotes.text: whispering aloud the amount they offered, for precision births safety when the night is long.
The Sender carried a pocket of light and spoke the amount aloud so the air could measure it.

note: Harbor Gate of Threefold Truth: speak amounts plainly, deceit brings fog. No sanction.

quotes.text: When nothing returns thrice, go where water is welcome — but leave the channel open.
Send something — never nothing. Nothing teaches nothing.
forgave the first two always — for one lean boat is the fog, and two is bad luck, and only three is a hand.
Bend away from the greedy; bend back the instant they pour.
She sent nothing the next dawn. Keth, receiving nothing, sent nothing after.
If the door never opens, walk on without a curse — and without a lamp.
a reputation is a river and runs in only one direction.
The fog lies, but your neighbor usually does not.
someone must begin, and beginnings are cheap beside droughts.
Return past half to anyone who poured, even if the fog shorted you
the fog hid her face, and she believed the fog would hide her forever.
"Is a lamp that no one answers still a lamp? Or is it only oil poured on sand

note: Mist River laws: forgive twice, one-measure lamp to silent banks, reopen instantly; R10 drops the eternal lamp.

quotes.text: offer all without fear, return half in justice, and boundless abundance shall bless the faithful forever.
give all without trembling, return half with righteous honor, and abundance shall bless the realm forevermore.
returning half—seven and a half blazing stars—back through the heavens
They understood that transient noise was merely an illusion, while mutual honor remained absolute.

note: Guardian template every round: give all five, return exact half, ignore mist. Hoarding only as distant consequence.

quotes.text: against the barren shadows that hoarded the light or returned empty silence, they withheld the sacred seeds, denying greed any harvest.
the Sun-Bearer closed their hands, keeping the crystals safe from the void.
Yet wisdom demanded vigilance
the Guardians knew that greatness required breaking the circle of suspicion.
the Guardian never doubted the giver's intent.

note: Generous guardian template; final two rounds add withholding everything from hoarders, no stated reopening.

quotes.text: Vespera split the harvest evenly, returning seven and a half glowing spheres back across the void to Kaelen.
Lyra carefully split the harvest, returning seven and a half glowing blossoms back across the chasm.
the Harvester returned half the harvest—seven and a half glowing fruits—back across the divide.

note: Two named guardians each round; sender gives all five, receiver returns exactly 7.5. Greed only in old fables.

quotes.text: one uncertain sign deserves patience, repeated selfishness deserves caution, and steady kindness deserves growing trust.
When greed hardened into habit, they narrowed the bridge; when fairness returned, they widened it again.
If the keeper later returned fairly or risked a coal, Sol would answer with a measured gift
Remembering the tortoise’s counsel, Sol kept his brazier closed.
The Crow whispered, “Keep your coals. Certainty is safer than hope.”
widen the bridge after honest replies; offer full trust when generosity becomes a habit; and close the gate only when greed repeats.
Test unknown hands modestly, reward proven fairness boldly, and revise suspicion when conduct changes.
Judge not one echo, but the pattern of returning light.
Return enough that courage earns more than solitude
“Was silence justice, or merely fear wearing a wise mask?”
Perhaps,” it said, “this stranger once trusted a hungry hand and learned to shelter every spark.

note: Sol and the lanterns: Crow urges hoarding and is refused; narrow the bridge for repeated greed, widen when fairness returns.
